observations.statement: Browser-capability rethink material is explicitly research input rather than direct implementation authority, and any canonical product or runtime change must first be transferred into an owning live Plans document.
PM-native orchestration owns parent and child supervision, timeout propagation, lineage, shell isolation, cancellation, and crew scheduling jointly with named shared contracts.

Every enumerated child lifecycle path must preserve run, thread, parent-run, and child-run lineage plus applicable requested and effective runtime descriptors, with parent oversight and audit visibility even for bridged providers.

Multi-turn child re-entry is restricted to explicitly supported continuation through PM-owned resume envelopes, must preserve narrowed-or-equal authority and runtime snapshots, and must not create hidden channels, implicit shared state, or an unbounded queue.

Child authority is clamped before dispatch and audited after completion across tool, write, FileSafe, mode, provider/model/account, and crew-admission dimensions; budget and terminal lifecycle outcomes share a canonical runtime taxonomy.
Task-tool delegation must enforce target-specific denial, reject unsafe self-dispatch, and retain lifecycle supervision for long-running tasks that return a session identifier.

Read-only subagent web and browser work is conditionally self-initiable only inside the parent permission ceiling, must route through named dispatch operations with lineage, reason, gates, visible cards, and evidence receipts, and remains advisory without artifact creation or permission escalation.
Questions and clarification are parent-owned: subagents escalate through the orchestrator and do not address users directly.
Child handoff context carries effective skill, tool, permission, and MCP snapshots plus cache, compaction, regression, and visibility context when those conditions affect the handoff.
AgentCard-style data is only an inspectable selection summary and cannot replace registry, authority, runtime-snapshot, or provider-capability contracts.

Elapsed-time terminal completion is named done.task_timeout, while pre-dispatch and post-response budget results remain in the budget taxonomy; done.timeout and alternate timeout headings are noncanonical.

The crew message board is the normative collaboration surface, with schema, routing, priority, rate limiting, orchestrator visibility, and parent mediation assigned to the orchestrator contract rather than UI projections.

Scheduling is graph-native and based on DAG readiness plus a scored ready set; tier and phase/task/subtask/iteration language is display or compatibility context, and lexicographic selection is retired.
Requested and effective account and role disclosure must carry through orchestrator, interview, and usage surfaces instead of being narrowed to a local packet.
Worktrees allocate by package by default, with policy-documented seam or lane exceptions; dependent nodes stay in the same lane unless promote-then-fork improves safe parallelism.

Selection fallback is declared deterministic: after capability filtering, the orchestrator chooses the next eligible candidate and records requested and effective Persona, selection reason, skipped controls, and relevant account-policy control context.
Turn, session, run, task, and subagent overrides are separate lifecycle records and cannot collapse into a sticky setting; execution_unit_context is the owner field over compatibility TierContext.
Every Orchestrator action must declare command-surface and bulk-safety metadata, and bulk mutation is disabled unless both command-catalog and permission contracts allow it.

GUI execution policy explicitly defaults retries to a fresh agent or subagent, permits same-agent context retention only by policy, defaults node workers to subagents, and records full-agent override as runtime policy.

Each failed node attempt emits a structured receipt and passes its handoff to the next subagent attempt; retry behavior is policy-driven and may route to remediation, graph patch, worker replacement, or human intervention.
Parallelism authority is package/seam lane-pool capacity rather than per-thread queues, per-provider caps, parallel subtasks, or crews per tier.
Replayable orchestration events go to the canonical seglog, run/session/checkpoint state goes to redb, and both writes are expected from the same orchestrator boundaries.

Run-start configuration merges GUI defaults, interview output, and per-tier overrides in later-wins precedence; scalars use last-writer-wins, arrays concatenate then deduplicate, objects deep-merge, and the result is validated before execution.
The optional interview test-strategy file contributes criteria and prompt excerpts; absence or invalidity is warning-only and execution continues with PRD or plan criteria.
Canonical orchestration identity is feature seam, work package, node, graph-generation lineage, and lane/worktree lineage; actors may share runtime identity semantics without becoming graph objects.
Provider selection requires a concrete frozen provider entry per node, OpenCode uses a server profile rather than an account row, and Copilot and Codex use direct-provider account rows.
Shared investigations remain subordinate to attempt and remediation lineage; workers may contribute to one investigation, and concurrent mutation of one project/worktree requires explicit isolation.

The project-context shape includes detected languages, frameworks, domain, optional task type, and error patterns; detected-language confidence is bounded by comment to 0.0 through 1.0, and domain and error-pattern enums enumerate their representable categories.
The ledger addendum explicitly does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, queues, implementation files, runtime dispatch, build tasks, generated governance artifacts, or a governance seal.

candidate_findings.title: Deterministic scheduler selection lacks a defined ordering oracle
candidate_findings.statement: The core declares a scored ready set and deterministic fallthrough to the next eligible candidate, but it does not define the score inputs, weights, tie-break order, candidate ordering, or stability rules that make those choices deterministic.
candidate_findings.impact: Conforming implementations can dispatch different nodes or providers from identical state, undermining replayability, audit comparison, and requested-versus-effective selection explanations.

candidate_findings.title: Seglog and redb consistency has no failure or atomicity contract
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires seglog appends and redb writes from the same orchestrator boundaries to keep state and events consistent, but it does not specify write ordering, transactionality, idempotency keys, crash recovery, or reconciliation after a one-sided failure.
candidate_findings.impact: A crash or partial write can leave replay history inconsistent with resumable state, with no stated authoritative side or repair procedure.

candidate_findings.title: Canonical config wiring retains tier-owned execution semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The core says live runtime policy is graph/package/seam/lane based and that Phase/Task/Subtask/Iteration is not canonical, yet the resolved run-start config still gives per-tier overrides highest precedence and validates through validate_config_wiring_for_tier().
candidate_findings.impact: Builders must choose whether tier-scoped configuration is authoritative or merely compatibility input, which can change effective model, effort, and provider settings for the same graph node.

candidate_findings.title: Composite config merge semantics are incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: Array concatenation and deduplication do not define equality keys or retained order, and object deep merge does not define null, deletion, type-conflict, or unknown-key behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Different merge libraries can produce different subagent lists and nested execution settings from the same three inputs.

candidate_findings.title: Config validation failure behavior is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires validate_config_wiring_for_tier() before execution but does not state its accepted schema, error payload, whether failure blocks dispatch, or what evidence is persisted.
candidate_findings.impact: Invalid effective configuration can be handled as a warning, fatal error, or silent normalization depending on builder choice, changing safety and reproducibility.

candidate_findings.title: Subagent web self-initiation gates leave consequential discretion
candidate_findings.statement: The web/browser rule depends on work being material and crawl/map work being bounded, but the core provides no materiality adjudicator, quantitative bound, denial behavior, receipt schema, or acceptance oracle for the required evidence.
candidate_findings.impact: Agents can make materially different cost, scope, privacy, and evidence-completeness decisions while claiming compliance with the same permission ceiling.

candidate_findings.title: Normative crew-board behavior is asserted without its contract
candidate_findings.statement: The core assigns crew-board schema, routing, priority, rate limiting, visibility, and parent mediation to this orchestrator contract but does not specify those fields, queue semantics, ordering, limits, delivery guarantees, or failure states in the assigned window.
candidate_findings.impact: Crew implementations can disagree on message delivery and supervision, producing dropped, reordered, starved, or unbounded collaboration traffic.

candidate_findings.title: Execution-limit admission authority is not concretely identified
candidate_findings.statement: The core rejects a stale numeric crew cap in favor of an executionLimits owner contract, but it does not identify an exact field or schema, state capacity units, or define admission denial, waiting, wake, and retry behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Concurrency enforcement can drift across crew and child admission consumers or recreate competing caps under different names.

candidate_findings.title: Post-completion authority audit has no violation outcome
candidate_findings.statement: The authority rule requires auditing after completion and recording post-response budget overrun, but the core does not define the audit oracle or the state, remediation, evidence, and user-visible result when a child exceeded effective authority.
candidate_findings.impact: A permission or budget violation may be merely recorded, retroactively rejected, quarantined, or accepted depending on implementation.

candidate_findings.title: Child context snapshot validity is undefined
candidate_findings.statement: The handoff carries cache, compaction, regression, visibility, and effective capability snapshots, but the core does not specify snapshot versioning, freshness, consistency checks, missing-field defaults, or rejection behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Resume and launch behavior can diverge when provider context shrinks or cached state conflicts with the effective permission envelope.

candidate_findings.title: Packet-emission fidelity has no executable acceptance oracle
candidate_findings.statement: Packet emission is blocked until contradictions in owner docs, runtime fields, and graph records are removed, but the core gives no validator, required evidence set, severity threshold, or authoritative pass/fail record for that condition.
candidate_findings.impact: One implementation can emit packets another blocks, allowing downstream execution from planning state whose fidelity was never deterministically established.

candidate_findings.title: Retry caps and remediation routing are underdefined
candidate_findings.statement: Retries are policy-driven with caps and can route to four distinct alternatives, but the core does not define cap units or defaults, retryable outcome classes, branch precedence, exhaustion behavior, or who may override the route.
candidate_findings.impact: Identical failed attempts can blind-loop, terminate early, replace workers, patch graphs, or escalate to human review inconsistently.

candidate_findings.title: Promote-then-fork exception lacks a decision rule
candidate_findings.statement: Dependent nodes stay in the same lane by default, but the exception applies whenever promotion then fork improves safe parallelism without defining the improvement metric, safety predicates, decision authority, or receipt.
candidate_findings.impact: Worktree placement and contamination risk depend on builder judgment and may not be replayable.

candidate_findings.title: Mutation-capable investigation exclusivity lacks lock lifecycle semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The core limits mutation-capable investigations per project/worktree unless isolated, but it does not define the admission key, lock acquisition, lease or heartbeat, stale-owner recovery, release point, or host-context equivalence.
candidate_findings.impact: Concurrent mutators may both be admitted or a crashed investigation may permanently block remediation.

candidate_findings.title: Project detection types lack derivation and fallback behavior
candidate_findings.statement: ProjectContext and its enums define representable data, but the core does not specify indicator collection, confidence calculation, multi-language conflict resolution, domain classification, thresholds, or how Unknown changes subagent selection.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent repositories can yield different project contexts and therefore different worker selection and prompts.

candidate_findings.title: Partially invalid test strategy handling is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The file-level missing or invalid case is warning-only, but the core does not define validation timing, partial acceptance of valid items, duplicate criterion handling, excerpt selection, or a persisted warning receipt.
candidate_findings.impact: Acceptance criteria can be silently lost, duplicated, or inconsistently injected into prompts.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: External bridge and A2A material is explicitly adapter guidance and is not authority to move PM-internal orchestration or budget and crew control onto A2A semantics.
Lifecycle lineage and parent audit visibility are explicit across spawn, retry, cancellation, timeout, pause, resume, and completion.
Resume authority is explicitly narrowed-or-equal and hidden channels, implicit shared state, and unbounded out-of-board queues are forbidden.
Unsafe self-dispatch is explicitly rejected, and a returned session_id does not detach a task from child lifecycle supervision.
The elapsed-time terminal name is explicitly done.task_timeout and is distinguished from budget outcomes.
GUI-visible retry identity and worker-class defaults are explicit, including the policy-gated same-agent option and recorded full-agent override.
The missing or invalid test-strategy file is explicitly nonfatal and falls back to PRD or plan criteria.
The canonical identity list and the rule that shared actor identity does not make actors graph objects are explicit.
Provider-row semantics are explicit for OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, and Codex node workers.
The single-mutator rule explicitly permits concurrency only when work is isolated to a separate worktree or host context.
The addendum's non-execution boundary explicitly excludes runtime and governance artifact creation.

unknowns.statement: The exact state and event members of the referenced canonical runtime outcome taxonomy are not present in the assigned core.
The exact executionLimits owner path, schema, and current capacity values are not identified in the assigned core.
The crew-board schema and its routing, priority, rate-limit, acknowledgement, and failure semantics are not present in the assigned core.
The ready-set scoring function and deterministic tie-break order are not present in the assigned core.
The authoritative packet-fidelity validator or acceptance receipt is not named in the assigned core.
The validation schema and failure result for validate_config_wiring_for_tier() are not present in the assigned core.
The recovery authority and reconciliation procedure for divergence between seglog and redb are not present in the assigned core.
The threshold and fallback consequences of a DetectedLanguage confidence value are not present in the assigned core.
The OSI-431 canonical_text continues syntactically at the context boundary after the word create, so its complete obligation is unknown within the authorized ranges.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: Browser-capability rethink entries in this planning-doc are research inputs, not direct implementation authority by themselves. They may survey capability breadth, behavior contracts and `/state` model, UX flows, safety and `/permissions`, and chat `/planning` integration, but canonical product/runtime changes must be transferred into the owning live `Plans/**` docs before implementation.

Internal multi-agent orchestration in Puppet Master is PM-native. Parent and child supervision, timeout propagation, thread and run lineage, shell isolation, cancellation, and crew scheduling are owned by this document together with `Plans/Contracts_V0.md` and `Plans/storage-plan.md`.

References to external bridge or A2A mapping material are adapter guidance only. They MUST NOT be read as approval for PM-internal child orchestration, child-run control messages, budget propagation, or crew coordination to move onto A2A semantics.

Every child spawn, retry, cancellation, timeout, pause, resume, and completion path MUST preserve PM lineage fields (`run_id`, `thread_id`, `parent_run_id`, `child_run_id`) plus requested/effective runtime descriptors where applicable. Parent oversight and audit visibility are mandatory even when a child is executing through a bridged provider surface.

Child sessions may be re-entered for explicitly supported multi-turn continuation only through PM-owned resume envelopes. Re-entry preserves lineage, narrowed-or-equal permissions, and current runtime snapshots; it does not create hidden inter-agent channels, implicit shared state, or an unbounded task queue outside the crew board contract.

Child effective-authority is clamped before dispatch and audited after completion. Parent restrictions clamp the canonical `child-permission` envelope: child tool policy, write scope, FileSafe scope, mode ceiling, provider/model/account availability, and crew admission. Pre-dispatch budget denial, post-response budget-overrun recording, completion, cancellation, kill, terminal cleanup, child-session / provider-process teardown, and `budget-outcome` supervision all use the same canonical runtime outcome taxonomy.

The stale later-stage example `Enforce maximum concurrent crews (e.g., 20 total)` from `Gap #45: Crew performance and scalability` is non-canonical. Crew and child admission use the executionLimits owner contract; no later-stage prose may reintroduce parallel caps that compete with that SSOT.

Task-tool delegation must honor per-target deny rules and must reject unsafe self-dispatch loops. A long-running task that returns a `session_id` is still governed by the same child lifecycle, resume, timeout, and parent supervision rules rather than becoming an unowned detached session.

Subagents may self-initiate read-only web/search/fetch/extract/research/deep-research/crawl/map work only within the parent-granted child permission ceiling and only when delegated source reading, bounded crawl/map, dynamic-page visual state, iframe/form evidence, console/network diagnostics, or source currentness is material to the assignment. These calls route through the PM WebOperation/BrowserAction dispatcher with `websearch`, `webfetch`, `webextract`, `webresearch`, `webcrawl`, `webmap`, or `BrowserAction/Site Reader`; each record carries `invocation_source = subagent`, required `agent_reason`, source_subagent_id lineage, permission/capability gates, visible operation cards, and `subagent_evidence_receipts`. Subagent web/browser evidence is advisory to the parent and must not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, runtime queues, implementation files, build tasks, hidden inter-agent channels, or permission escalation beyond the parent envelope.

Task and question escalation remain parent-owned. Subagents may request clarification only by escalating through the parent orchestrator; they do not address users directly, and task alignment follows the parent `/question` flow plus the child lifecycle contract instead of a child-local ask channel.

Child launch context carries a normalized effective skill/tool/permission/MCP snapshot plus cache-affinity, cache-hit, compaction-state, compaction-regression, and subagent context visibility context when provider-side caching, ordinary compaction, or dynamic context shrinking affects the handoff. These are propagation inputs to the PM child-run record and handoff bundle; they do not create provider-specific hidden channels or bypass the parent permission ceiling.

AgentCard-style capability advertisement is allowed only as an inspectable capability summary for PM subagent selection. AgentCard data does not replace the registry, permission ceiling, runtime snapshot, or provider capability contract.

The legacy duplicate heading string `#### Task-envelope timeout contract` is retired as a separate live heading. The singular child timeout envelope above is the non-contradictory owner contract: terminal elapsed-time completion is `done.task_timeout`, while pre-dispatch and post-response budget outcomes follow the budget taxonomy. Any wording that under-specifies or over-summarizes this by reviving `done.timeout` or alternate timeout headings is non-canonical.

The crew message board is the normative subagent-collaboration surface. BrainStorm, Crew, and Assistant projections may show collaborative summaries, but schema, routing, priority, rate limiting, orchestrator visibility, and parent mediation remain owned by this orchestrator contract.

The scheduling model is graph-native: runnable graph nodes, DAG readiness, scored ready-set selection, and runtime-selection use plan-graph, plan_graph, project_plan_graph_index, project_plan_graph_index.schema.json, plan_graph.schema.json, `/project/plan_graph/index.json`, puppet-master/project/plan_graph/index.json, `/node`, `/node/runtime`, node shard files, and sharded-only execution inputs. Any `Phase / Task / Subtask / Iteration`, Phase, Task, Subtask, Iteration, tier_id, active-tier, TierChanged, tier-scoped, tier-keyed, tier-native, runnable-unit, or TierContext language is derived display or compatibility context only. Lexicographic-style selection is retired in favor of the scored ready-set.

Runtime identity carry-through is mandatory across orchestrator, interview, and usage. Plans/usage-feature.md, /usage-feature.md, Plans/interview-subagent-integration.md, /interview-subagent-integration.md, Plans/orchestrator-subagent-integration.md, /orchestrator-subagent-integration.md, execution_unit_context, requested_account_policy, requested_account_binding, persona_override_owner_id, plan_or_tier_default, SSOT, `select_for_tier()`, select_for_tier, account_id, requested_account_id, operational_identity, runtime-identity, runtime-role, billing-identity, `/account-history`, `/effective`, tool_use_id, and carry-through fields must preserve requested/effective account and role disclosure rather than narrowing to one local packet.

Worktree allocation is package-based by default with seam/lane exceptions documented by policy. SCM and /worktree behavior uses Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md, /WorktreeGitImprovement.md, package-based lane pools, branch-per-tier compatibility notes, contamination quarantine, restore-before-reuse, same-cycle event-driven update, file-lease rejection, first-class `/update`, `/backoff`, steady-state avoidance, worktree-native isolation, and safe-point-aware `/transition` recovery. Dependent nodes stay same-lane by default; promote-then-fork occurs only when it improves safe parallelism.

Packet emission is gated by target-level fidelity. Packet artifacts may be useful planning state, but they are not faithful-emission-safe until packet-planning inputs remove contradictions in owner docs, target-level runtime fields, and /graph scheduling records. The orchestrator therefore treats packet-planning as a preflight contract, not as proof that downstream packet emission can proceed.

Scheduler and account selection fallbacks are deterministic. Graph scheduling uses package-based /graph lane pools, /capacity-aware ready-set filtering, blocked constraints, and wake reasons before dispatch. If a preferred subagent, Persona, provider, or /provider/model candidate is unavailable after capability filtering, the orchestrator falls through to the next eligible candidate while recording requested Persona, effective Persona, selection reason, skipped Persona controls, and any requested_account_policy /control frame that explains how selection occurred.

Scoped overrides have explicit lifecycle boundaries: turn, session, run, task, and subagent overrides are separate records and must not collapse into one sticky runtime setting. TierContext is retained only as a compatibility wrapper that may carry legacy_decomposition_context beside canonical execution_unit_context; storage-side runtime consumers and human-in-the-loop projections must treat execution_unit_context as the owner field.

Orchestrator action metadata is `command-owner` bound to `Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md` / `UI_Command_Catalog`: every Orchestrator action declares whether it is `palette-visible`, `shortcut-worthy`, `context-menu` only, `bulk-safe`, or `bulk-forbidden`, and bulk mutation remains disabled unless the catalog and permission contracts both allow it.

GUI `execution-policy` settings choose retry identity and node worker class explicitly: default retries use a fresh agent/subagent, optional same-agent retries retain prior context only when policy allows, and node execution uses `/subagent` workers by default with a full-agent override recorded as runtime policy rather than hidden state.

Retry and remediation preserve `structured-attempt-handoff`: each failed node attempt emits a receipt of what it did, what changed, why it failed or was `/blocked`, and what to try next. Retries remain policy-driven with `/caps`; some outcomes route to remediation, graph patch, `/worker` replacement, or `/HITL` instead of blind looping, and the `/handoff` artifact remains attached to the next `/subagent` attempt.

Parallelism uses package/seam `lane-pool` capacity rather than stale `per-thread` queues, `per-provider` caps, parallel subtasks, or crews-per-tier as execution owners. Those older shapes may appear only as migration notes that map into package/seam promotion and lane capacity.

This plan remains authoritative for subagent selection policy and wiring/verification requirements. Any tier policy phrasing from Phase/Task/Subtask/Iteration is compatibility/source-lineage only; live runtime policy is graph/package/seam/lane based. As the rewrite lands (see `Plans/rewrite-tie-in-memo.md`):

- **Seglog:** Emit to the canonical seglog stream: tier start/end, iteration start/end, verification results, subagent invocation boundaries, and any event that must be replayable. Use the unified event model; do not add one-off log files for run history.
- **redb:** Persist in redb (per storage-plan.md schema): orchestrator **run** metadata (run id, PRD ref, status, timestamps); **session** identity and linkage to run; **checkpoints** at phase/task/subtask boundaries for resume and recovery. Config used by the run is built at run start per Option B (see config-wiring below).
- Implementation: run/session/checkpoint writes and seglog appends should be called from the same orchestrator boundaries (e.g. after verification, on tier advance) so state and event stream stay consistent.

At run start, the orchestrator builds the full execution config by merging three sources in this precedence order (later overrides earlier):
1. **GUI config defaults** (from redb `config:gui.*`): platform, model, effort, plan_mode defaults.
2. **Interview output config** (from interview artifacts): subagent assignments, phase config, research settings, technology-specific overrides.
3. **Per-tier overrides** (from PRD/plan tasks): any task-level overrides for platform, model, or effort.

Merge rules:
- Scalar values: last writer wins (per precedence).
- Arrays (e.g., `subagents`): concatenate and deduplicate.
- Objects: deep merge (per-key override).

The merged config is validated by `validate_config_wiring_for_tier()` before execution begins.

- Orchestrator loads `.puppet-master/interview/test-strategy.json` if present.
- Merges `items[].criterion` into tier acceptance criteria and injects relevant excerpts into prompt context.
- Missing/invalid file is WARN-only (no crash); continue execution with PRD/plan criteria only.

The rewrite no longer treats `Phase -> Task -> Subtask -> Iteration` as the canonical orchestration ontology.

Canonical orchestration identity is:
- `Feature Seam`
- `Work Package`
- `Node`
- graph generation lineage
- lane/worktree lineage

Rules:
- any surviving phase/task/subtask language is derived decomposition/view language only
- conversational actors, interview actors, and document builders may share runtime identity semantics with orchestration actors without becoming graph objects
- worktree ownership, recovery, approval, usage, and routing must align to run/node/attempt/lane/worktree identity rather than to `tier_id`

This legacy section is retained for import/search compatibility. Live runtime
subagent routing uses GoalRun, WorkGraph, WorkNode, package, seam, lane, phase,
capability_lane, agent_role, SubagentWave, and SubagentPolicy vocabulary. Terms
such as tier, phase/task/subtask/iteration tier, tier_overrides, and
enable_tier_subagents are compatibility aliases only and must normalize through
`SubagentPolicy` before runtime admission.
Canonical worker strategy remains graph-owned rather than tier-owned, but provider/runtime selection for node workers must now use the reconciled runtime ontology.

This heading is retained as a compatibility/search anchor. Canonical worker strategy is capability-lane and graph/package/seam/lane owned, with tier labels permitted only as legacy projection or migration vocabulary.

Required orchestration rules:
- node execution selects from the same provider-entry / account-or-profile model used elsewhere in the rewrite.
- the orchestrator may request a provider family pool, but the frozen requested/effective runtime snapshot must still identify the concrete provider entry selected for each node worker.
- OpenCode subagent execution selects a server profile, not an account row.
- GitHub Copilot and Codex subagent execution use direct-provider account rows rather than legacy CLI assumptions.
- orchestrator-side skill and MCP behavior follows the PM-native skill/MCP model and does not require provider-specific native skill delivery contracts.

Orchestrator may launch shared investigations when builds, tests, environment setup, or runtime verification fail.

Required rules:
- Orchestrator does not switch into the Assistant `Debug` mode strip; instead, it uses the same shared investigation contracts and debug-capable tools under orchestration ownership
- investigation state remains subordinate to the owning attempt / remediation lineage rather than replacing orchestrator run identity
- delegated workers may contribute evidence, traces, or fixes to the same `investigation_id` when they are operating on the same issue
- only one mutation-capable investigation may target the same project/worktree at a time unless the orchestrator explicitly isolates work in a separate worktree or host context

pub struct ProjectContext {
    pub languages: Vec<DetectedLanguage>,
    pub frameworks: Vec<String>,
    pub domain: ProjectDomain,
    pub task_type: Option<TaskType>,
    pub error_patterns: Vec<ErrorPattern>,
pub confidence: f32,        // 0.0-1.0

pub enum ProjectDomain {
    Backend,
    Frontend,
    FullStack,
    Mobile,
    Infrastructure,
    Data,
    Embedded,
    Unknown,

pub enum ErrorPattern {
    CompilationError,
    TestFailure,
    SecurityIssue,
    PerformanceIssue,
    RuntimeError,
}

It does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, implementation files, runtime dispatch, production build tasks, generated governance artifacts, or a governance seal.

canonical_text: >-
  Subagents and agent harnesses may receive containerized-host capability context only under the parent goal, run mode,
  execution_unit_context, worktree/jail policy, permission snapshot, FileSafe scope, and host assignment ceiling inherited
  from the supervising PM surface. Child agents can consume host_capability_ref, host_profile_id, host_assignment_id,
  host_execution_receipt, cleanup_retention_receipt, and blocker payloads, but they cannot bypass parent authority, create
